name: AGE OF EXPLORATION
clue: After Magellan died in the Philippines, this Basque navigator sailed the Victoria home, completing the first circumnavigation in 1522

name: PEN NAMES
clue: Author Eric Blair took his famous pen surname from an English river he loved to walk beside

name: ACCIDENTAL PRESIDENTS
clue: He's the only person to serve as both U.S. vice president and president without being elected to either office

name: FINAL EPISODES
clue: Over 100 million Americans watched 'Goodbye, Farewell and Amen,' the 1983 finale of this Korean War sitcom

name: OPENING SENTENCES
clue: 'Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way' opens this Tolstoy novel

name: NOBEL PHYSICS
clue: Einstein's 1921 Nobel Prize cited his explanation of this effect, not his theories of relativity

name: STELLAR NEIGHBORS
clue: This red dwarf, with a name meaning 'nearest,' is the closest star to our sun

name: WORLD CUP HISTORY
clue: In 1930 this nation of some 2 million people hosted the first FIFA World Cup and won it too

name: CAPITAL NAMESAKES
clue: Liberia's capital city honors this U.S. president, whose namesake doctrine warned European powers away from the Americas

name: DUTCH MASTERS
clue: Centuries of darkened varnish on his 1642 daytime militia portrait earned it the misleading nickname 'The Night Watch'

name: CHEMICAL SYMBOLS
clue: Its symbol W comes from Wolfram, its German name; no metal melts at a higher temperature

name: TRIPLE CROWN
clue: At a mile and a half, this 'Test of the Champion' is the longest of horse racing's Triple Crown races

name: RING RECORDS
clue: In 1956 this heavyweight champion retired with a perfect 49-0 record, a mark no heavyweight titleholder has matched

name: THE CONSTITUTION
clue: It's the only constitutional amendment ratified specifically to repeal an earlier amendment

name: WORLD WAR II
clue: Clouds over the primary target of Kokura diverted the second atomic bomb to this city in August 1945

name: ISLAND NATIONS
clue: Earth's fourth-largest island is the biggest occupied entirely by a single country that shares its name

name: PLANETARY NAMES
clue: Alone among the eight planets, this one takes its name from Greek rather than Roman mythology

name: LOGO LEGENDS
clue: The dribbling silhouette in the NBA's logo was modeled on this Lakers guard nicknamed 'Mr. Clutch'

name: DOUBLE LAUREATES
clue: This American chemist is the only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes: Chemistry in 1954 and Peace in 1962

name: AFRICAN COASTLINES
clue: It's the only African nation with shores on both the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean

name: CARBON COPIES
clue: Like diamond, this soft gray mineral that fills pencils is an allotrope of pure carbon

name: SHAKESPEARE'S ROMANS
clue: Banished by the city he had saved, this general marches an enemy army to Rome's gates in the Shakespeare tragedy named for him

name: DRAWING THE LINE
clue: This 1494 treaty drew a meridian through the Atlantic, dividing newly found lands between Spain and Portugal

name: COLD WAR CHESS
clue: In Reykjavik in 1972, this American ended a 24-year Soviet grip on the world chess championship

name: ORGAN RECITAL
clue: This human organ can regrow to full size from as little as a quarter of its original mass

name: THE PERIODIC TABLE
clue: Element 98, first created in 1950 at a university cyclotron, takes its name from the state where it was made

name: UNITS OF MEASURE
clue: The SI unit of magnetic flux density honors this inventor, born in 1856 in what is now Croatia

name: AND THE OSCAR GOES TO...
clue: This 1969 tale of two New York hustlers is the only X-rated film ever to win the Best Picture Oscar

name: CALENDAR LOGIC
clue: September means 'seventh month' — a name that made sense when the early Roman year began in this month

name: EPIC TITLES
clue: Homer's epic of the Trojan War takes its title not from its hero but from this alternate name for Troy
